question: What is the primary medical reason a patient receives a standard cardiac pacemaker?

options.A: To measure the exact blood volume in the heart
options.B: To stop a fast ventricular fibrillation
options.D: To remove plaque from blocked coronary arteries

explanation: Pacemakers are primarily used to deliver electrical impulses when the heart beats too slowly and causes symptoms like dizziness. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T9#GNS321_U2_T9_h1)

question: How does a standard pacemaker actually assist the heart muscle?

options.A: By sending tiny electrical pulses to prompt regular contractions
options.B: By pumping blood directly through plastic tubes into the aorta
options.C: By delivering high-energy shocks to restart a stopped heart
options.D: By permanently replacing the heart valves with mechanical gates

explanation: The device acts as an artificial electrical conductor, firing small pulses to make the heart muscle contract at a safe rate. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T9#GNS321_U2_T9_h1)

question: What is a dual-chamber pacemaker designed to do?

options.A: Pace both an atrium and a ventricle
options.B: Store two separate batteries for emergencies
options.C: Pace the left and right lungs together
options.D: Monitor blood pressure and breathing rate

explanation: A dual-chamber system uses two leads to coordinate contractions in both upper and lower chambers of the heart. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T9#GNS321_U2_T9_h2)

question: How does a demand pacemaker operate during a normal heart rhythm?

options.A: It pumps extra blood to compensate for the fast natural rhythm
options.B: It shuts down completely and must be manually restarted by a doctor
options.C: It continuously sends rapid shocks to speed up the normal heartbeat
options.D: It remains idle and only fires when the natural heart rate drops too low

explanation: Demand pacemakers monitor the heart's natural electrical signals and only step in when the rate falls below the programmed threshold. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T9#GNS321_U2_T9_h2)

question: Which medication group requires careful review before a pacemaker insertion due to bleeding risks?
explanation: Blood thinners increase the risk of bleeding into the surgical pocket where the pacemaker battery is placed. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T9#GNS321_U2_T9_h3)

question: A nurse is getting a patient ready for a pacemaker insertion. What is the very first thing that must be done?

options.A: Shave the entire chest wall from nipple to neck
options.B: Program the pacemaker to a high heart rate
options.D: Verify that the informed consent form is signed

explanation: Making sure the patient understands the procedure and signs the consent form always comes first before any physical preparation begins. Well done! [learn more](GNS321_U2_T9#GNS321_U2_T9_h3)

question: What is the main activity restriction for the affected arm right after pacemaker insertion?

options.A: Avoid writing or holding objects with that hand
options.B: Keep the arm pressed tightly against the stomach
options.C: Do not raise the arm above shoulder height
options.D: Do not bend the elbow past ninety degrees

explanation: Lifting the arm too high can pull the newly placed wires loose from the heart muscle wall. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T9#GNS321_U2_T9_h4)

question: Why do nurses monitor patients on continuous telemetry right after a pacemaker is put in?

options.A: To measure the exact daily battery drain of the internal computer
options.B: To confirm that every electrical spike successfully triggers a heart contraction
options.C: To record the patient's blood pressure changes during sleep
options.D: To detect any airborne infections entering the surgical wound

explanation: Telemetry lets you check 'capture'—meaning you verify that the device's electrical signal is actually making the heart beat. You're thinking like a real nurse! [learn more](GNS321_U2_T9#GNS321_U2_T9_h4)

question: Which finding at a pacemaker incision site should you report right away as a sign of infection?

options.A: Mild itching around the healing skin
options.B: Faint bruising fading to a yellow color
options.C: A small firm lump directly under the scar

explanation: Pus and spreading redness are classic warning signs of an infection that needs prompt medical attention. Excellent clinical eye! [learn more](GNS321_U2_T9#GNS321_U2_T9_h5)

question: Why should patients with a pacemaker avoid contact sports?

options.A: High impact activities cause the heart rate to become permanently fixed
options.B: Rapid arm movements will completely drain the battery within a few hours
options.C: Physical blows to the chest can damage the generator or dislodge the wires
options.D: Sweating during heavy exercise will rust the titanium case of the battery

explanation: Hard blows to the chest can break the wires or shift the device out of place. Protecting that pocket is key! [learn more](GNS321_U2_T9#GNS321_U2_T9_h5)

question: What does a pacemaker 'failure to capture' mean?

options.A: Pacing spikes show on the monitor, but the heart does not beat in response
options.B: The device fails to notice the patient's own heartbeat and fires at the wrong time
options.C: The wires disconnect from the skin surface outside the chest wall
options.D: The internal battery runs out completely and the heart stops instantly

explanation: Failure to capture means the pacemaker is sending out the signal (the spike), but the heart muscle isn't responding to it. You are getting the hang of ECG concepts! [learn more](GNS321_U2_T9#GNS321_U2_T9_h6)

question: A patient with a pacemaker feels dizzy, and the monitor shows a malfunction. What is your immediate nursing priority?

options.A: Place a strong magnet directly over the incision to turn off the pacemaker
options.B: Instruct the client to raise the left arm above the head to reset the wires
options.C: Notify the healthcare provider and ensure emergency equipment is ready
options.D: Give a large dose of oral pain medication to calm the patient down

explanation: When a patient feels dizzy and the device malfunctions, act fast: notify the doctor and get emergency gear ready. Patient safety always comes first! [learn more](GNS321_U2_T9#GNS321_U2_T9_h6)

question: Which common household appliance is completely safe for a patient with a pacemaker to use?
explanation: Good news for patients—standard household microwaves are well-shielded and won't mess with modern pacemakers. One less thing to worry about! [learn more](GNS321_U2_T9#GNS321_U2_T9_h7)

question: How should an airport security check be handled for a passenger with a pacemaker?

options.A: Turn off the pacemaker completely using an external switch before entering the security line
options.B: Walk through the metal detector normally, but ask security to avoid using a hand-held wand over the chest
options.C: Show the medical card and demand a full body cavity search instead of walking through arches
options.D: Refuse all security screening because airport machines will instantly destroy the pacemaker

explanation: Walking through the security arch is usually fine if you keep moving, but security should avoid holding a magnetic wand directly over the chest. Practical knowledge for clinical practice! [learn more](GNS321_U2_T9#GNS321_U2_T9_h7)

question: What is the primary purpose of regular pacemaker interrogation appointments?

options.A: To surgically replace the battery every six months
options.B: To reprogram the heart muscle to beat much faster
options.C: To check battery life and evaluate device functioning
options.D: To wash the surgical scar and apply fresh bandages

explanation: Interrogation allows healthcare providers to assess remaining battery power, lead performance, and device data. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T9#GNS321_U2_T9_h8)

question: Why is emotional and psychological support an important part of long-term care for pacemaker patients?

options.A: Emotional support prevents the pacemaker leads from coming loose in the heart
options.B: Mental stress directly drains the electrical battery inside the chest wall
options.C: Psychological counseling is legally required before every battery replacement
options.D: Patients often experience anxiety and fear regarding device failure or lifestyle limits

explanation: Living with a device in your chest can be scary. Being a supportive nurse means caring for their emotional worries just as much as their physical heart! [learn more](GNS321_U2_T9#GNS321_U2_T9_h8)
